$comment: CALLOUTS: what ecu's rules decide to say, from every source (live, replay-<run>, parity), for radio to speak (ADR 0001, point 1; paddock#73). ecu decides; radio only speaks what it reads here.
subjects: twr.v1.*.callout.> covers contracts' callout.p0, .p1 and .p2, twr.v1.<src>.callout.<level>.
retention workqueue (ADR 0001): a callout is said once, so the consumer's ack removes it; nothing reads callouts afterwards.

max_age 30 s (30000000000 ns): a callout is worth saying only while it is current. 30 s, not ADR 0001's 15 s, as decided in the triage of paddock#73: the race summary's own expiry is 30 s, so the stream never ages out what a rule still allows.

duplicate_window 30 s (30000000000 ns): the callout's id is its Nats-Msg-Id (contracts' subjects.yaml), so one sent again is stored once. paddock#73 asks for 2 min, but the server refuses a duplicate window longer than max_age (error 10052), and a callout older than 30 s is gone anyway.
max_bytes 64 MiB (67108864): a callout is a few hundred bytes and lives 30 s, so the stream holds a few KB. The limit is a backstop so a stuck consumer cannot fill the disk.
discard old: if the backstop is ever reached, the oldest callouts, the stalest, go first.
max_msg_size -1: bounded by the server's max_payload (1 MiB by default). max_msgs, max_msgs_per_subject and max_consumers -1: max_age and max_bytes are the limits.
num_replicas 1: one NATS server (ADR 0004). File storage so a callout raised just before a server restart is still said.
name: CALLOUTS
description: Callouts from every source for radio, kept 30 s or until acked, deduplicated on Nats-Msg-Id (paddock#73).
